_comment: Audio-tag placements for the eleven_v3 read of the appointed-time VO. Read by automation/clarity_tag.py, which emits a tagged script ALONGSIDE the clean one — never instead of it.
_why_a_separate_file: Audio tags are an eleven_v3 feature. On eleven_multilingual_v2 a bracketed tag is either spoken aloud as literal text or ignored, so a tagged script handed to the wrong model is worse than no tags at all. Keeping the tagged variant separate means the model choice stays a choice.
_this_set_is_deliberately_strong: 88 placements across 3,579 words — one per 41 words, against 31 across 5,861 (one per 189) on the revelation-order script. That is roughly four and a half times denser, and it was asked for. The cost is real: v3 is more expressive AND less deterministic than v2, and this script is generated in 17 separate batches that have to sound like one person. Every placement therefore carries a weight: 'core' or 'extra'. Run the generator with --level core for the restrained 48-placement / 82-tag set, and --level strong (the default) for all 88 placements and 126 tags. Audition batches 01, 09 and 17 back to back at strong before committing to it; if they do not sound like the same reading, drop to core, and if core still drifts, use v2 and the clean script.
_vocabulary: v3 interprets bracketed direction contextually rather than from a fixed enumeration, so these are requests, not switches, and the same tag reads differently in different sentences. Every one must be auditioned.
_subject_limits: No [laughs], no [shouting], no [sarcastic], no [excited], no [crying]. This is a Quran channel and the register is a serious explainer. Strong here means precise and weighted, not performed. Two further limits are absolute rather than stylistic: NO TAG TOUCHES A RECITATION INSERT — those six places are a real reciter and never TTS at all — and no tag sits on an English rendering of an ayah except [measured], because a narrator emoting through a translation of scripture is the exact thing this channel's 'AI BE AWARE' comment is pointing at.
_pacing_tags_carry_most_of_the_strength: [pause], [long pause], [slows] and [almost a whisper] are doing more work here than any emotional tag. Breath and rate are what make a twenty-seven minute faceless read hold, and unlike an emotional direction they cannot swing the performance between batches. That is why 41 of the 88 placements carry a pacing tag rather than emotion alone.
_placement_rule: NO TAG MAY OPEN A BATCH, or open a paste block after a recitation insert. A tag at position 0 is the model's strongest, most literal reading of it — there is no preceding prose in that generation to moderate it — and it fires exactly at the seam where the previous audio ends, so every join gets an audible restart. Worse, it marks nothing: a tag sits where the register turns WITHIN a reading, and at the top of a block there is nothing to turn from. The generator refuses to build if any placement lands at position 0.
_anchor_rule: Each tag is inserted immediately BEFORE its anchor string, matched against the batch's REFLOWED text (the clean script hard-wraps at 100 characters, so anchors routinely span a line break). Every anchor must appear EXACTLY ONCE in its batch or the generator fails loudly rather than inserting in the wrong place or silently not inserting at all.
_emphasis_rule: CAPS is v3's emphasis mechanism. Nine single words are raised, listed under 'emphasis'. Seven of them are already **bold** in the clean script — the bold marks where the writer wanted stress, and CAPS is how v3 receives it. Never raise a multi-word Arabic phrase: v3 reads an all-caps transliteration unpredictably, sometimes letter by letter.
